The read

The honest framing isn't "what's the best practice" — it's "what does the Joule experience tell you to do differently before you wire Workday Recruiter Agent or Oracle Fusion agents into the stack." AR-04 is your live case study, and it's underperforming: $0.8M measured against $1.4M target after 9 months, adoption 10% against 77%, POS integration at 31% against 45% target. The pressure card flags a $900K realization gap at MED confidence.

The deployment pattern that's failing AR-04 is the one most teams default to: turn on the vendor-built agents, assume embedded = adopted, discover the data/integration layer isn't ready, watch value lag.

What the corpus actually says about Workday's model

Workday's pitch at Rising 2024 is the Agent System of Record — a registry/lifecycle/governance plane where you "manage agents the way you manage workers: hire, role-assign, monitor, retire" [Workday newsroom — Agent System of Record, 2024-09]. First-party agents (Recruiter, Expenses, Succession, Optimize, Talent Mobility, Contracts) are gated on it. That's the vendor's stated deployment frame, not consensus advice.

For Apex specifically, two governance hooks already apply: NY Local Law 144 requires pre-deployment review if Workday introduces AI in hiring (Recruiter Agent would trigger this), and the AI Governance Council has tier-2 pre-deployment authority [compliance_posture.md § compliance].

Three things Tower would push on before any ERP-agent deployment

1. Data/integration readiness gates the value, not the agent. AR-04's POS feed is the bottleneck, not Joule itself. The pending decision is to defer action-layer expansion until POS clears — with finance and merch in dissent. That's the pattern: don't expand agent scope while the substrate is incomplete.

2. Baseline + measurement method before turn-on. Tower's value grounding shows no canonical pattern for this question, and AR-06 (cost attribution) is still at 38% coverage. You don't yet have the measurement plumbing to attribute Workday or Oracle agent value cleanly.

3. Governance registry, not just vendor toggles. Workday's ASR concept maps to what your AI Governance Council already does — use case inventory, tier-2 review, attestation. If you adopt Workday agents, the ASR shouldn't replace your council; it should feed it.

Hand-off

The actual strategy choice — whether to deploy Workday/Oracle agents at all, and in what sequence relative to the erp program — belongs in Sentinel or an ERP-future program charter. the erp program is in scoping with the decision held; agent strategy should be sequenced inside that, not ahead of it.

Want me to draft the question set Sentinel should answer before any ERP-agent deployment, or pull AR-04's lessons-learned into a pre-deployment checklist?
